A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoRegEmbed. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching; v1 Appendices A–B are retained and expanded in v3, which adds Appendices C–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original STS experiments, trained comparison baselines, component and loss ablations, and learning-efficiency experiments in Tables 1–2 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v3 reports original STS and retrieval results, together with ablations of similarity functions, alignment strategies, and temperature parameters in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The core information-compression architecture and conditional-distribution alignment loss remain. However, v3 Section 4.1 introduces a retrieval-specific adaptation: an additional epoch of conventional contrastive fine-tuning. The newly explicit inner-product inference description does not establish a changed inference procedure.

E1.justification: v3 extends evaluation from ten STS datasets to document retrieval on MS MARCO, NFCorpus, and SCIDOCS, and adds MS MARCO training. The existing PWC-Unique and NLI training coverage remains; naming the NLI sources MEDI and BGE clarifies existing data rather than adding datasets.

E2.justification: The corresponding STS and existing ablation comparisons retain their comparator membership. The new retrieval table reuses previously evaluated methods: supervised and unsupervised LLM2Vec, SFR-Embedding-2_R, gte-Qwen2-7B-instruct, and LLaMA2-inbatch-M. Newly discussed generative predecessors are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A changes the reported default temperature tau from 0.1 to 0.05, keeping beta at 0.1. The new retrieval protocol uses nDCG@10, additional contrastive fine-tuning, and seven hard negatives sampled from NV-Embed ranks 30–210. v3 also adds the larger-data Mistral configuration and explicit temperature-search experiments.

E4.justification: New Appendices C, E, and F test Tanh versus Sigmoid, four alternative alignment strategies, and sensitivity to tau and beta. These substantially expand the investigation of design choices beyond v1's component and Log-Sigmoid/KL/JS ablations. Conversely, the epoch-efficiency experiment shown in v1 Figure 3 is removed; the sample-efficiency analysis remains.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests, including in the appendices. The reported averages aggregate datasets, not repeated runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises AutoRegEmbed scores alongside the temperature change: the 50,000-sample LLaMA2 ten-dataset average changes from 83.07 to 83.24, while 83.07 remains reported for tau=0.1 in v3 Appendix F. A new 274,951-sample Mistral row reports 84.59. New retrieval results are 42.49, 38.16, and 19.79 on MS MARCO, NFCorpus, and SCIDOCS. Tables 4, 6, and 7 add analysis results, while the epoch-wise results disappear.

T1.justification: The core mathematical objectives remain, but Appendix E adds explicit formulations of four alternative alignment losses in Equations 3–6. Section 3.3 removes v1's formal alignment and uniformity definitions. These are bounded changes to mathematical definitions and variants; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: two autoregressive training tasks producing effective embeddings with fewer examples and performance comparable to SOTA. Section 4.2 reports a stronger STS ranking, but the central contribution and headline claim scope remain.

C2.justification: v3 changes the Sigmoid rationale from matching cosine-distance ranges to preventing exponential overflow. It newly discusses the training/inference mismatch in asymmetric retrieval and interprets cross-dataset retrieval differences. Appendices B–F add a KL/JS instability hypothesis, explanations of alignment choices, and an interpretation that tau and beta effects may interact. The standalone safety limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 supplies exact STS and retrieval instructions in Table 5, names the existing NLI sources, clarifies reference probabilities and inner-product inference, and documents retrieval negative mining. Most implementation information was already present in v1, including five compressed tokens, learning rates, hardware, training times, and code links.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces its early-model isotropy and multi-stage discussion with generative predecessors coCondenser, PaSeR, and RetroMAE, distinguishing their supervision and model scale from AutoRegEmbed. Introduction and dataset citations expand, while references including Su et al. 2021, Ni et al. 2022, and Wang et al. 2022 disappear. The broader research positioning remains.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the introduction, related work, and Section 3.3, plus a retrieval subsection and new appendix sections. Instruction explanations are reorganized into Appendix D, and author and acknowledgment text changes. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the displays with retrieval Table 2 and appendix Tables 4–7. Table 1 gains a model row and ranking emphasis; the original ablation table becomes Table 3 and moves. Figure 3 changes from two full-width panels to a single-column sample-efficiency plot, removing the epoch panel.

improvement.justification: The retrieval evaluation and new function, alignment, and temperature studies better support applicability and design choices, while exact instructions improve reproducibility. These gains are qualified by the additional contrastive stage needed for retrieval and removal of the epoch-efficiency evidence. A new inconsistency also remains: Table 3 reports 83.24 versus 73.90, but the prose retains the old 9.17-point difference instead of 9.34. Overall, the evidence supports a useful but limited net quality improvement.
